title: The Journey of a Raindrop

requirements.goal: Create a short original animated classroom story in which a teacher teaches and students listen, think, answer, and celebrate learning together.
requirements.audience: Children ages 8-13, teachers, parents, and general short-form viewers.
requirements.lesson: A simple, scientifically accurate introduction to evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.

output.captions: Burned in plus editable SRT sidecar

requirements.narration: Warm, natural female teacher voice with one short student response; measured pacing with scene holds instead of accelerated speech.
requirements.sourceStrategy: Original generated fictional character and classroom artwork, local deterministic animation, locally generated music, neural speech, and no downloaded stock media.

creativeDirection.visualStyle: Original high-end 3D children's educational animation with rounded shapes, tactile clay-like materials, expressive faces, warm cinematic classroom light, and clean readable staging.
creativeDirection.pacing: Six clear story beats lasting roughly 9-12 seconds each, with a visual action change every 2-4 seconds through restrained camera motion and layered educational graphics.
creativeDirection.composition: Characters stay large in frame; the teacher, listening students, board, and lesson object remain readable on a phone. Captions stay within the Shorts/Reels safe area.
creativeDirection.animation: Subtle Ken Burns camera movement, short dissolves and directional reveals, animated water-cycle icons, restrained character emphasis, and no shaking or uncontrolled floating.
creativeDirection.music: Original cheerful classroom score with soft marimba-like notes, rounded bass, gentle hand-clap texture, and no harsh stingers.
creativeDirection.textPolicy: No generated in-image text. All labels and captions are rendered deterministically by the video pipeline.
avoid: copyrighted characters or recognizable franchise styles

cast.description: Fictional South Asian woman in her early thirties with warm brown skin, shoulder-length dark wavy hair, a mustard cardigan over a teal blouse, navy trousers, and small round gold earrings. Calm, encouraging, and expressive.
Fictional Black boy, age 10, short coiled hair, cobalt-blue hoodie, curious and attentive.
Fictional Arab girl, age 10, dark braid, coral headband, cream top with green overalls, thoughtful and confident.
Fictional East Asian girl, age 9, chin-length black bob, round glasses, lavender sweatshirt, observant and cheerful.
Fictional white boy, age 11, freckles, tousled auburn hair, yellow T-shirt under denim overalls, energetic but respectful.

storyboard.visual: Wide vertical classroom view. Ms. Maya welcomes the class while four students settle at curved desks and turn toward her. A large blank interactive board sits behind her.
storyboard.action: Gentle push-in; teacher raises one hand; students look up and settle.
storyboard.narration: Good morning, explorers! Today we're following one tiny raindrop on an amazing journey through the water cycle.

storyboard.visual: Ms. Maya points to a bright illustrated sun above an ocean and puddle on the board. Students lean forward and watch.
storyboard.action: Slow pan toward the board; question mark and small water-drop icon appear as deterministic overlays.
storyboard.narration: When sunshine warms oceans, lakes, and puddles, where does the water go? Watch closely.

storyboard.visual: Close classroom teaching view. A tabletop bowl of water glows gently under a safe demonstration lamp while vapor arrows rise toward the board. Students observe with wonder.
storyboard.action: Upward camera drift limited to three percent; translucent arrows rise once; students' eyes follow the vapor.
storyboard.narration: It becomes invisible water vapor and rises. This is evaporation—the sun gives water energy to climb into the sky.

storyboard.visual: The interactive board shows vapor cooling into tiny droplets and forming a fluffy cloud. Ms. Maya gestures across the sequence; students listen closely.
storyboard.action: Soft left-to-right reveal; tiny droplets assemble into one cloud; no repetitive looping.
storyboard.narration: High above us, cooler air turns vapor into tiny droplets. They gather into clouds. This is condensation.

storyboard.visual: A friendly cloud diagram releases rain, snow, and tiny hail icons on the board. Amina raises her hand while the other students stay focused.
storyboard.action: Short rain streak reveal; camera eases toward Amina's raised hand; teacher nods.
storyboard.narration: When clouds become heavy, water falls as rain, snow, or hail. This is precipitation, returning water to Earth.

storyboard.visual: The whole class gathers around a completed circular water-cycle display. Amina answers, Ms. Maya gives a thumbs-up, and the students smile as a tiny raindrop travels around the loop.
storyboard.action: Circular line traces once; brief student close-up, then a warm wide ending; final raindrop settles at center.
storyboard.narration: Can anyone complete the cycle? Evaporation, condensation, precipitation—and collection, as rivers, soil, and oceans gather the water. Exactly! Water keeps traveling around and around. Every drop has a story.

workflow: Persist this production plan before generating media.
Generate and inspect one cast anchor image.
Generate six portrait scene plates using the cast anchor as the identity and style reference.
Generate scene-level neural narration and measure the real audio duration.
Build the final scene timeline from measured narration plus readable holds.
Generate original procedural music and an SRT caption sidecar.
Assemble a schema-v2 creator manifest with restrained motion and short transitions.
Render the native 1080x1920 master and thumbnail.
Inspect encoded frames, safe zones, audio levels, duration, and delivery profile.
Package the video, captions, thumbnail, manifest, plan, resource list, and QA report.
qualityChecklist: Teacher and all students remain visually consistent across all six scenes.
Every frame clearly shows teaching, listening, thinking, answering, or celebrating learning.
The water-cycle sequence is scientifically accurate and narration matches the visible lesson beat.
No generated text is relied upon; deterministic labels are spelled correctly.
Faces, hands, and classroom objects have no obvious generation artifacts at phone viewing size.
Captions use no more than two lines and stay above the Shorts/Reels bottom UI area.
No important face, board element, label, or caption touches the unsafe edge regions.
Motion is smooth and deliberate with no shaking, flashing, or uncontrolled floating.
Voice remains natural and music stays below narration without harsh transient sounds.
Final duration remains between 60 and 75 seconds at 1080x1920 and 30 fps.
H.264 video, AAC audio, thumbnail, SRT, checksums, and provenance are present.
assumptions: A general English-language educational story is appropriate because no curriculum, age, or language was specified.
One vertical master can be uploaded unchanged to both YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels.
The requested cartoon can use 2D/2.5D motion over original generated scene plates; phoneme-level lip sync is not required.
All people are fictional and no real child identity is represented.
